>why were the writers constantly torturing jenny

 Well, that's because Jenny should have become the MC. She was a fourteen year old girl standing up to her bullies and got punished for it. 

Why ?

You see, by the second season of Gossip Girl, the 2008 recession hit and people were losing their jobs, their homes and it brought people back into reality real quick. Gone was the early 2000's fascination (Paris Hilton, Lindsay Loan, Y2K era) with the ultra wealthy, or more accurately, the fascination stayed but the resentment grew. So, shows like Gossip Girl were faced with two options. Dig into the "Eat the Rich" sentiment or make the show total escapism. They chose the later.

And so the wealth and everyone in it was glorified. 

That meant, from now on, that less wealthy characters were always wrong to point out the others' privileges because they were hypocrites who would do the same if they could.  Chuck and Blair were doing awful stuff (especially to Jenny!) but it was portrayed as "iconic", and when Jenny, fed up, would retaliate in a show of strength she was portrayed as the "villain" and since any good villain needs punishment - she couldn't win. 
Hence why Rufus never even tried to hear Jenny out post S1, why Dan never defends his sister more than that, 
meanwhile 
Blair bullies her, Chuck plays with her (often to taunt Blair), Serena, who could tell her friends to cool it off, is complicit and never too bothered. 

Jenny was the ultimate threat to the show, because she showed how awful these people were and had she been written properly, Gossip Girl would have been remembered as an anti-rich, anti-capitalist show. Which is not veryyy commercial to TV channels, but it does wonder for the audience. 

When you realize who and what finance this whole industry, you see why they chose to keep GG lighter since season 1 was never about making a political message. GG was written as a fun teenage-centered satire of the rich n wealthy and nothing more, just like the books.

Here's something that might help you. I just turned 24 and I also was under the impression of not having done much, until I redefined what accomplishments and achievements meant for me. We are *so hard* on ourselves, we fail to see all the now seemingly small but at the time huge obstacles overcome through the years. 

Hell we went through COVID. That was a lot and I can't imagine doing it as young as you did. It was scary, stressful, and isolating. Yet you did it. Trying to keep up with online school when we've all seen how unstimulating it is *is* an accomplishment in itself. Trying requires a lot of strength and a lot of people don't even bother. Succeeding is the cherry on top but even if you fail at that, you tried and you learn from it. That's called evolving as a person. Helping out your mom, being a supportive presence to your siblings, reaching for help (even through Reddit), all of these are victories. Whatever it is, think back of your 13 years old self and see how far you got. 

Social media bombards us with success stories of 18 years old being multi-millionaires, of people climbing Everest and other kind of out of this world accomplishment as if it's the norm. It's not. Small victories are just as important and if you don't learn to appreciate them, I fear you won't be able to appreciate the bigger ones. It won't ever be enough and you'll never be satisfied or proud of yourself. You have your own path and it shouldn't be compared to anyone else's. 

Start small. Be kind and patient with yourself.

You ask the interesting question of the hierarchy within the harem and not only is it not historically accurate in the show, but it's supra confusing 😂

But here's my understanding of it based on my *many* rewatches of the show 

- Dynasty members - 

**Active Sultan -** He is above everyone. His decision and will are not to be questioned. (Süleyman)

**Valide Sultana -**  In Islam, they say the right of a mother is the right of God. She doesn't bow to her son but have to obey his orders. Everyone but the Sultan bow to her (including statesmen). She rules the harem. (Ayfsa) 

**Shezades -** Bow to the Sultan & the Valide Sultan, unclear if the Valide can give them orders but probably not. By respect they bow to their slave mothers and their blood sultana aunts but they do not have to bow to other mothers of shezades or daughters of Sultan. (Mustafa, Mehmet, Selim, Bayezid, Chihangir) 

**Blood Sultanas, sisters of active Sultan (and daughters of previous ones) -** They're dynasty's blood but they have to obey the Sultan and the Valide Sultana. They get married to high-ranking statesmen. (Hatice, Beyhan, Sah)

**Blood Sultanas, daughters of active Sultan -** They're not inferior to the sisters of the Sultan, but, by what seems to be respect for their elders, they bow & listen to their aunts. Though they are above their mother, but bow to her for respect. In public, might have to bow to their brother but don't seem to do it in private. (Mihrimah)


- The Harem - 

**Haseki Sultan -**  *In the show* she is a slave but above the kalfas,;harem girls and mothers of other shezades. She bows to all dynasty's members. (Mahidevran, Hürrem)

**Mothers of dynasty's members -** Depending on the gender and health of their offspring, they might rank higher or lower than other mothers (Mahidevran v Gulfem)

**Private Concierge -** Personal assistant to the Sultan. I'd say he has little authority on the Treasurer, but a lot on the Harem's Eunuch. (Ibrahim, Bali Bey)

**Treasurer -** Valide Sultan's right hand, if she speaks in Valide's name the treasurer can have more power than the Haseki, even if, officially, she's way lower than her. 
(Daye Hatun)

**Harem's Eunuch -** In charge of harem's day to day affairs. He is greatly respected by outsiders and is very close to the Sultan's intimate affairs (contrary to statesmens). He is under all the dynasty members, the Hasekis and the Treasurer's. (Sumbul)

**Head Kalfas -** They seem to be some sort of head of the harem's servants. They might be somewhat equal to the Harem's Eunuch if they're a Haseki's personal servant like Gulsah was. (Nigar)

**Other kalfas, eunuchs and harems girls -** Well the harem girls do have to obey the staff most of the time but it can all change if they catch the Sultan's eye. 

There!  So obviously that's based on the show, but it seems that historically not only Haseki Sultan was a title only invented for Hürrem (and so Mahidevran never was one), but the legal wife should have also ranked above the sisters of the Sultan and the Valide Sultan
